source.title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders for Monosemantic Representation
source.authors: Moghis Fereidouni; Muhammad Umair Haider; Peizhong Ju; A. Siddique

record.tranche_reason: The study measures concept overlap and activation-distribution separability in model neurons and SAE features, offering a different operationalization of monosemanticity from the claim’s audit of named neuron poles.
record.gate_note: The study tests concept overlap and separability, not the proportions of poles assigned one job, two related jobs, or not understood. Figure 1 reports overlap results for all model-and-dataset combinations; only some values are stated in text, so the rest are recorded as figure only. Figure 6 reports overlap for active SAE neurons. Table 7's DeepSeek entries are too flattened to assign values reliably. Intervention results are omitted because they assess concept-erasure methods, not the claim versions’ neuron-job shares. Figures 2 and 5 and Table 6 give examples of activation patterns, not a separate aggregate estimate of neuron-job shares.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It measures how often the top-80 salient hidden-state dimensions are shared across coarse dataset labels (topics, POS, NER, emotions), and a Jensen–Shannon separability score per dimension. It compares Gemma-2-2B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B with their SAE latents. Its 'neuron' is a component of the hidden-state vector; interventions sit after the MLP and residual addition in the final block. These are residual-stream dimensions, not MLP neuron poles. Nothing is audited for 'one main job': a unit with a clean job unrelated to the dataset labels would still score as overlapping or low-separability. No share of one-job, two-job or not-understood units is reported, and there is no InceptionV1, attribution-graph or simulation-scoring work. This is a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAEs reduce polysemanticity (less label overlap, higher JS separability) relative to base models, though polysemantic units remain. Wider SAEs, and sparser SAEs at equal width, separate better. SAEs also allow more precise partial concept erasure. Their APP method gives the smallest perplexity increase while staying competitive at removing the target concept.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures concept overlap and Jensen–Shannon separability across labelled datasets; it does not conduct a pole-by-pole explanation audit or classify poles into one job, related jobs, or not understood.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, SAE width, and SAE l0/sparsity are varied; the paper reports that higher-capacity SAEs generally show lower overlap and greater separability.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2-2B, the top-80 salient hidden-state dimensions overlap across labels: ~38% for POS and ~9% for DBpedia. Base-layer JS separability is 0.31–0.41 versus 0.39–0.71 for GemmaScope SAEs. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B base is 0.29–0.44 versus SAE 0.60–0.72.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-stream dimensions of dense LMs separate coarse labelled concepts (topic, POS, NER, emotion) less than SAE latents do. Wider and sparser SAEs separate them more.

record.code_released: Code will be released publicly after paper acceptance.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study uses labelled concepts from five datasets and does not estimate the claimed shares of one-job, two-related-job, or not-understood poles. The overlap analysis focuses on the top 80 salient neurons; the broader all-active-neuron analysis is only for SAEs. Quantitative concept-erasure table results are single representative runs, although selected reruns are described as consistent.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 repeats Gemma values shown in Table 7 and is not duplicated. DeepSeek values in Table 7 are not assigned because the provided table text is too flattened to identify them reliably. Concept-erasure tables and related results are omitted because they assess intervention performance rather than the claimed neuron-job shares.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B, no pole-by-pole job audit, no 90/7/2–4% shares.
All: no share of one-job neurons in any model; no MoE or trillion-scale models; units are residual-stream dimensions, not MLP neurons.
All: InceptionV1 cat/car, pose, recursive generalization.
All: architecture, regularization and tools as causes; vision-model estimates.
All: attribution graphs on neurons versus replacement models.
All: activating-example explanations versus held-out firing prediction.
All: simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

missing.what: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B JS separability, readable in order: base 0.367, 0.291, 0.436, 0.325, 0.366 and SAE 0.597, 0.643, 0.718, 0.698, 0.698 (dataset assignment per column order POS, AG News, Emotions, DBpedia, NER).
Figure 1 bars for 65k POS, 16k and 65k DBpedia are not recorded.

record.verdict_notes: The record overclaims a test of V1/V2. The study's 'neurons' are hidden-state (residual) dimensions judged against dataset labels, which cannot show whether a unit has one main job. SAE rows describe a trained replacement basis, not the model's neurons. Its framing assumes polysemanticity is common; it does not measure the claim's construct.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B audit and its specific estimates of about 90% one-job poles, about 7% two-related-job poles, and about 2–4% not understood; the study instead uses concept overlap and separability measures on other models and datasets.

The claimed shares across other models are not directly estimated. No mixture-of-experts or trillion-parameter model is tested; the named models are Gemma-2-2B and a DeepSeek-R1 distilled 8-billion-parameter variant.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, and recursive generalization.
Architecture, regularization, tool-quality explanation, and the InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
Attribution graphs and whether neurons suffice as circuit units without replacement models.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples fail to predict held-out firing.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B base-model neurons on the tested concept datasets
reader_labels.reason: The reported base-model POS overlap is around 38%, and its separability scores are below the SAE scores; these measures qualify the broad monosemanticity claim but do not directly reproduce the Qwen pole categories (F1-base-pos, JS-gemma-base-pos, JS-gemma-base-agnews, JS-gemma-base-emotions, JS-gemma-base-dbpedia, JS-gemma-base-ner).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The tested Gemma SAE variants and concept datasets
reader_labels.reason: Separability is higher for the tested SAE variants than for the Gemma base model, with different scores across datasets and SAE settings; this is not a direct estimate of similar neuron-job shares across models (JS-gemma-base-pos, JS-gemma-16k116-pos, JS-gemma-16k285-pos, JS-gemma-65k93-pos, JS-gemma-65k197-pos).
